title: Dedicated serve commitment: sliding-window error budget & burst-absorption contract playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Produce a contract-ready playbook and template clauses that define a quantitative dedicated throughput commitment using a sliding-window error budget, a burst-absorption allowance, and explicit remediation triggers. This ticket consolidates legal language, measurement definitions, SLO math, and the operational runbook for incident crediting and escalations.

Scope:
- Define the primary SLA metric (Committed Serve Rate) with measurement windows and query semantics.
- Specify the sliding-window error budget mechanics (window size, quantiles, and rollup behavior).
- Introduce Burst-Absorption Allowance as a negotiated cushion that permits short-term over-commit consumption without immediate credits.
- Produce contract language for notice windows, remediation ladder, service credits computation, and optional escrowed credit accounts.
- Align autoscaler interlock behavior and operator-runbook so that autoscale actions do not invalidate credit audits.

Out of scope: pricing negotiation and legal sign-off (legal review is required but sign-off is separate).

Deliverables:
1) Contract appendix text (boilerplate clauses) in plain-language and legal-ready versions.
2) Measurement spec (time-series query, aggregation, thresholds).
3) Example incident credit calculation with synthetic dataset.
4) Runbook mapping alerts -> mitigation -> credit computation -> customer communications.

Why this differs from prior drafts: Instead of single-window quantile guarantees or fixed token-per-minute floor, this playbook uses a sliding-window approach (e.g., 30m window sampled every 5m) to better capture transient spikes and correlate with autoscaler behavior. The burst-absorption concept formalizes temporary over-consumption handling that we previously treated informally in on-call notes.
acceptance_criteria: Legal-ready contract appendix text exists in both plain-language and redline forms
Measurement spec includes exact PromQL/SQL queries and example results
Runbook has clear owner, SLT contact, and escalation timeline
Automated credit computation examples match manual audit for three synthetic incidents

2025-03-05: Design review (Jules Patel) suggested adding customer-facing examples in the contract annex to reduce ambiguity. Assigned to PM to draft three examples: planned maintenance, short spike due to dependent service, sustained degradation over 2 hours.
notes: Key trade-offs discussed: tighter sampling intervals increase false positives (leading to unnecessary credits) vs. coarser intervals mask short client-impacting spikes. The sliding-window quantile approach reduces sensitivity to single outliers while preserving responsiveness. Burst-Absorption reduces churn on credits for transient spikes but must be limited to avoid masking capacity regressions.
operational_runbook: Step 1: Detection - alert when Committed Serve Rate 99th percentile over 30m sliding window drops below agreed floor. Step 2: Triage - on-call verifies autoscaler logs and pod/container health. Step 3: Mitigation - trigger configured autoscaler policies (scale-up or fallback to compatible variant). Step 4: Credit decision - if burst-absorption allowance covers the deficit, mark incident as 'absorbed' and no credit. If not, calculate credit per appendix and notify customer within 48 hours. Step 5: Post-incident - populate audit sheet and recompute sliding-window samples for the billing period.
example_credit_calculation: Example: Customer committed 10k tokens/min sustained. SLA floor defined as P95 >= 9.5k tokens/min over sliding 30m window sampled every 5m. Billing cycle 30 days. Incident: sustained deficit averaging 8k tokens/min for 40 minutes, with a 10-minute spike below 5k for unrelated infra event. Burst-Absorption set to 15% per billing cycle. Compute deficit area under curve, subtract absorbed portion, prorate credits as % of monthly invoice per appendix formula.
